Create a Color Range Between Two Colors

Source: R/create_color_range.R
create_color_range.Rd

Generate a sequence of colors by interpolating between two endpoint colors. If a single color is supplied, that color is repeated.

Usage

create_color_range(color_palette, n, single_color = "middle")

Arguments

color_palette

A character vector containing one or two colors in a format understood by grDevices::col2rgb(), such as hexadecimal color codes or R color names. With two colors, these define the endpoints of the generated range.

n

A positive integer specifying the number of colors to generate.

single_color

Character string defining which color is returned when n = 1 and two endpoint colors are supplied. One of "middle" (default), returning the color between both endpoints; "first", returning the first endpoint; or "last", returning the second endpoint.

Value

A character vector of length n containing hexadecimal color codes.

Details

When two endpoint colors are supplied, colors are generated by interpolation between the endpoints using colorspace::mixcolor(). Both endpoint colors are included when n > 1.

When only one color is supplied, it is repeated n times.

When n = 1 and two endpoint colors are supplied, single_color determines which color represents the range. By default, the midpoint between both endpoint colors is returned.

Examples

# Define a set of colors between two endpoints
create_color_range(c("#2166AC", "#B2182B"), 5)
#> [1] "#2166AC" "#45538C" "#6A3F6C" "#8E2C4B" "#B2182B"

# Assign a color to multiple entries
create_color_range("steelblue", 3)
#> [1] "#4682B4" "#4682B4" "#4682B4"

# Select a single color from a range
create_color_range(c("#2166AC", "#B2182B"), 1)
#> [1] "#6A3F6C"
create_color_range(c("#2166AC", "#B2182B"), 1, single_color = "first")
#> [1] "#2166AC"
create_color_range(c("#2166AC", "#B2182B"), 1, single_color = "last")
#> [1] "#B2182B"
